newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just higher on short covering.

text.p: Gold came under pressure in early European business on Friday as many houses went short looking to force the pace on the downside, dealers said.

However at the fixing cover buying had taken gold back up to $337.30 per ounce against the Thursday afternoon fixing of $336.95 which reflected selling mainly from Europe in the immediately aftermath of the over the counter option expiry.
"That was entirely expected but the fall this morning after gold was steady in New York and the Far East was surprisingly quick," a dealer said.
Dealers aid it was mainly selling from London and Europe which took both the Tokyo and Hong Kong closes below New York and straddling $337.00.

The Hong Kong close was also affected by the dollar firming against the yen and thin trading conditions ahead of the Hong Kong markets closing until Thursday while the territory reverts to Chinese rule.
"The downtrend is still in progress but the market has been held up by physical support at $337.00," a dealer said, adding that if the physical buying dried up then the downside would be tested.
There was " a good chance" that the February 12 four-year low of $336.15 would come into play in that case, the dealer said.
But good technical support was forecast at the low which could lead to a bounce to $337.50-$338.00 keeping gold in the very narrow range seen for the past three days.
Whether or not that goes on for much longer was debatable, a market analyst said.
The Monsoon season was already upon India and likely to stifle demand and was moving into South East Asia.
"Typically you would expect to see gold fundamentally in balance at this time of year," the analyst said.
Silver was a couple of cents lower at $4.75/$4.77 and showing little inclination to move significantly and the PGMs were also fairly steady, dealers said.

Several dealers said the report rollover after Swiss interests failed to deliver a call option to a U.S. counterparty at Thursday's expiry probably amounted to no more than the option writer agreeing to borrow the metal for a month.
"At a 50 percent one-month lease rate that's good business," a dealer said. Palladium was quoted at 80 percent.
Platinum was about $1.00 lower at $416.00/$419.00 and palladium $2.00 down at $194.00/$199.00.
